symptoms: Yellow pustules arranged in linear stripes/striping along leaf veins. Dust of yellow powder comes off on fingers when touched.
favorable_conditions: Cool and humid weather (temperatures between 10°C to 15°C with heavy morning dew or light showers).
prevention_and_treatment: Grow resistant varieties such as HD 3086, DBW 187, DBW 222, PBW 725, or Unnat PBW 343.
Monitor fields regularly in January-February in Northern India (Punjab, Haryana, Tarai region).
Chemical control: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) @ 1 ml per liter of water (200 ml in 200 liters of water per acre) or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L at first appearance.
Avoid excess nitrogen fertilization which makes foliage succulent and prone to infection.
organic_treatment: Spray 5% Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE) or Sour Buttermilk (Chhachh) mixed with copper vessel extract as a preventive measure in early stages.
source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal

symptoms: Spindle-shaped or eye-shaped lesions with brown or reddish-brown borders and grey/ash-colored centers on leaves. Neck rot causing empty panicles.
favorable_conditions: High relative humidity (>90%), intermittent drizzle, night temperatures around 20-24°C, excessive nitrogenous fertilizers.
prevention_and_treatment: Seed treatment with Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 2g/kg of seed before sowing.
Avoid excessive split doses of Urea; maintain balanced N:P:K (120:60:40 kg/ha).
Foliar spray of Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L at early tillering and panicle emergence stage.
organic_treatment: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens powder @ 10g/L or bio-agent Trichoderma viride seed treatment.
source: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack

symptoms: Early Blight: Concentric rings (target board pattern) on older leaves. Late Blight: Water-soaked dark brown irregular lesions with white fuzzy mold under humid conditions.
favorable_conditions: High moisture, cloudy days, cool temperatures (15-22°C for Late Blight; 24-29°C for Early Blight).
prevention_and_treatment: Ensure proper crop spacing (at least 60x45 cm) and staking for good airflow.
Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L preventively.
Curative action for Late Blight: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP (Ridomil MZ) @ 2.5g/L water.
organic_treatment: Spray Copper Hydroxide @ 2g/L or Trichoderma harzianum; prune bottom leaves touching the soil.
source: Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru

symptoms: Rosetted flowers, young bolls shed, lint stained brown, punctured bolls with internal larvae feeding on seeds.
favorable_conditions: Mid to late season (60-120 days after sowing) with dry warm intervals.
prevention_and_treatment: Install Pheromone traps @ 5 traps/acre for monitoring and 15 traps/acre for mass trapping.
Spray Profenophos 50% EC @ 2ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5g/L when trap catches exceed 8 moths/trap/night.
Do not extend the crop duration beyond 150-160 days.
organic_treatment: Release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre at weekly intervals starting at flowering; spray 5% Neem oil (1500 ppm) @ 5ml/L.
source: ICAR - Central Institute for Cotton Research (CICR), Nagpur

symptoms: Nitrogen deficiency causes general yellowing of older leaves. Phosphorus deficiency causes purplish foliage and stunted roots. Potassium deficiency causes leaf margin scorching.
favorable_conditions: All seasons; dependent on Soil Health Card testing.
prevention_and_treatment: Conduct soil testing before every cropping season under the Soil Health Card scheme.
Standard balanced recommendation: Cereals (4:2:1 NPK ratio), Pulses (1:2:1 NPK ratio with Rhizobium inoculant).
Incorporate 2-3 tonnes of decomposed Farm Yard Manure (FYM) or Vermicompost per acre 2-3 weeks before sowing.
Apply full Phosphorus and Potassium at sowing; split Nitrogen into 2-3 doses (basal, tillering, jointing/flowering).
organic_treatment: Use green manuring with Sesbania (Dhaincha) or Sunhemp; apply Azotobacter/Azospirillum and Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) @ 250g/acre.
source: Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) & IARI, New Delhi

symptoms: Water stress symptoms: wilting during midday, leaf curling, premature flower and fruit drop.
favorable_conditions: Dry spells, high temperature periods, summer crops.
prevention_and_treatment: Adopt Drip Irrigation for row crops (vegetables, cotton, sugarcane) saving 40-60% water while improving yield by 20-30%.
Use Sprinkler Irrigation for closely spaced crops like wheat, mustard, pulses, and groundnut on undulating lands.

Irrigate wheat at critical physiological stages: 1. Crown Root Initiation (CRI) at 21 days (most critical), 2. Tillering (40-45 days), 3. Late jointing (60-65 days), 4. Flowering (80-85 days), 5. Milking (100-105 days).
organic_treatment: Apply organic straw or plastic mulching to reduce soil water evaporation and suppress weeds.
source: Water Technology Centre, ICAR-IARI, New Delhi
